kept.title: Unrestricted Temporary File Creation
kept.description: The DiskStorage engine uses os.tmpdir() by default without verifying storage path permissions or rotation, potentially leading to disk exhaustion or sensitive file exposure in shared environments (lib/storage/disk.js:19).
steps_to_exploit: Identify a server running with default DiskStorage settings
Send numerous multipart requests with large file payloads
Observe the server disk space usage increase until failure or temporary files clutter the system
kept.impact: Denial of Service (DoS) due to disk exhaustion or potential unauthorized access to uploaded files if the OS temporary directory permissions are misconfigured.

kept.title: Lack of Global File Count Limit
kept.description: While specific field limits exist, there is no global constraint on the total number of files across all fields, allowing an attacker to exhaust memory or file handles (lib/make-middleware.js).
steps_to_exploit: Create a multipart request with a vast number of small files spanning multiple field names
Bypass field-specific limits by spreading files across many unique keys
Monitor server memory/CPU usage as it attempts to process all parts
kept.impact: Resource exhaustion leading to service downtime.

kept.title: Prototype Pollution via append-field
kept.description: The application uses 'append-field' to parse nested object structures. Without explicit sanitization of field names, an attacker could potentially inject properties into Object.prototype (lib/make-middleware.js:230).
steps_to_exploit: Craft a multipart request with a field name like '__proto__[polluted_prop]'
Submit the request to a route using this middleware
Check if the server's global object has been modified
kept.impact: Potential Remote Code Execution (RCE) or application-wide logic bypass via prototype pollution.

kept.title: Denial of Service via Request Body Draining
kept.description: The middleware attempts to 'drain' streams (lib/make-middleware.js:33) upon error, which can be weaponized by an attacker sending extremely large requests that force the server to constantly read and discard input.
steps_to_exploit: Trigger a validation error early (e.g., file size limit)
Send a massive, endless stream of data
Server continues reading the entire stream to satisfy the 'drain' requirement, consuming I/O and CPU
kept.impact: CPU and I/O exhaustion, causing the server to be unresponsive to other users.

kept.title: Insecure Error Handling of File Streams
kept.description: File stream errors are caught and trigger an abort, but the cleanup process in removeUploadedFiles involves sequential setImmediate calls, creating a race condition window (lib/remove-uploaded-files.js).
steps_to_exploit: Initiate multiple large uploads
Force a failure mid-upload
The cleanup routine may lag, leaving orphan files on the filesystem longer than intended
kept.impact: Disk space bloat and potential leakage of sensitive file fragments.

kept.title: Unbounded Array Index Expansion
kept.description: Despite a regex check in exceedsArrayIndexLimit, the limit logic is opt-in (via options) and can lead to sparse array creation if the 'fieldArrayIndexLimit' is not configured appropriately (lib/make-middleware.js:27).
steps_to_exploit: Craft a field name with a very high index, e.g., 'data[99999999]'
Submit request without specific fieldArrayIndexLimit protection enabled
Observe the server allocating memory for a sparse array of massive size

kept.title: Default Use of Latin1 Encoding
kept.description: The middleware defaults to 'latin1' for parameter charset if not specified, which can lead to data corruption or character set confusion when processing non-English filenames (index.js:22).
steps_to_exploit: Upload files with UTF-8 non-ASCII filenames
Observe the characters being misinterpreted or replaced by the middleware during processing
kept.impact: Integrity loss of filename data, which may be exploited for bypass of security filters looking for specific file extensions.

kept.title: Potential File Descriptor Leakage
kept.description: In lib/storage/disk.js, there is an edge case where 'close' might not fire for a stream, causing the WeakMap to hold references longer than needed (storage/disk.js:50).
steps_to_exploit: Generate high-concurrency requests that trigger stream errors
Observe if the WeakMap or file descriptors are not being garbage collected correctly
kept.impact: File descriptor exhaustion, leading to the server failing to open new files.

kept.title: Insecure Random Filename Generation
kept.description: Using crypto.randomBytes(16).toString('hex') is generally safe, but the storage/disk.js implementation allows overriding this, which could lead to predictable filenames if improperly implemented by users (storage/disk.js:13).
steps_to_exploit: Supply custom 'filename' function in DiskStorage configuration
Ensure the user function returns predictable strings (e.g., timestamps or sequential IDs)
Perform targeted lookups on the temporary folder
kept.impact: Unauthorized access to files via filename guessing.

kept.title: Exposure of Internals in MulterError
kept.description: The MulterError class exposes specific internal error codes (e.g., 'LIMIT_UNEXPECTED_FILE') to the client, potentially assisting in reconnaissance (lib/multer-error.js:21).
steps_to_exploit: Send malformed or disallowed multipart requests
Inspect the JSON error response provided by the API
Identify server-side configuration limits through the error codes
kept.impact: Information disclosure helping attackers tune their payloads to bypass specific security limits.

kept.title: Race Condition in indicateDone()
kept.description: The logic in lib/make-middleware.js:137 relies on multiple state booleans (readFinished, pendingWrites) to trigger 'done'. If multiple async callbacks overlap incorrectly, it may cause premature invocation of the next() middleware.
steps_to_exploit: Send a high-concurrency request with overlapping field and file streams
Attempt to access req.files before the storage engine has fully resolved the writes
kept.impact: Application-level logic errors where the middleware thinks processing is complete when it is not.

kept.title: Lack of Validation on 'destination' Path
kept.description: The DiskStorage constructor allows providing a custom 'destination' string. If this is sourced from user input, it leads to Arbitrary File Write (lib/storage/disk.js:25).
steps_to_exploit: If the app constructs DiskStorage({ destination: userInput }), pass an absolute path outside the intended directory
Upload a file to overwrite critical system files or config

kept.title: Over-reliance on 'type-is' for Middleware invocation
kept.description: The middleware uses 'type-is' (lib/make-middleware.js:68) to verify 'multipart' content type. If the application is behind a proxy that strips or manipulates headers, this could be bypassed or trigger misrouting.
steps_to_exploit: Send a non-multipart request with a manipulated Content-Type header to confuse the middleware
Observe if the middleware incorrectly attempts to process the request as multipart
kept.impact: Bypass of security checks and potential crashes in the underlying Busboy parser.

kept.title: Memory Leak in PendingFiles Queue
kept.description: If a request fails after files are added to pendingFiles but before removal, the array may retain object references (lib/make-middleware.js:102).
steps_to_exploit: Trigger repeated aborts during file uploads
Monitor heap usage for object retention
kept.impact: Slow memory leak over time in high-traffic applications.

kept.title: Insecure 'Any' Strategy usage
kept.description: The .any() method creates a strategy that accepts everything, which is often used incorrectly by developers who forget to implement custom filters, leaving systems open to file uploads (index.js:77).
steps_to_exploit: Identify an API endpoint utilizing multer.any()
Upload arbitrary files including sensitive executable types (e.g., .js, .php, .exe)
kept.impact: Unrestricted file upload vulnerability leading to malware or shell deployment.
